modules.title: 负载增加时，延迟和错误率怎样越过阈值
一次负载测试怎样产生有用证据

items.title: 先把测试条件写成可重复的场景
items.text: 只说“模拟很多人”不够。要说明用户动作、负载规模或请求速率、持续时间、测试环境和数据类型；接近生产的环境与合成或脱敏数据才能让结果更接近真实判断，同时避免碰到真实用户数据。

items.title: 让指标决定下一轮动作
items.text: 测试记录延迟、吞吐量和错误率，并与事先约定的阈值比较。若结账在负载增加时变慢或失败，先定位瓶颈并改善，再用相同场景重测；结果改善说明这项变更有效，但只覆盖被测场景和条件。

items.title: 第二个场景：在线课堂
items.text: 开课前模拟学生同时进入直播间并提交答题，按目标人数记录进入延迟、提交吞吐量和错误率，再用相同条件复测改善结果。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 负载测试关注目标或预期负载下系统怎样表现；压力测试通常把负载继续推高以观察极限或失效方式，两者目的不同。一次负载测试通过，只说明这次环境、数据、场景和时间范围内的结果，不能证明生产所有流量、依赖和故障组合都不会出问题。

lessonPractice.title: 活动前的结账负载测试显示，p95 延迟（95% 请求的响应时间不超过这个值）已经超过阈值，错误率也在上升。哪种处理最有用？

options.label: 保留测试场景和指标，定位瓶颈，改善后重复测试并比较结果
options.feedback: 对。负载测试的价值在于用可重复的负载和阈值发现瓶颈，再用下一轮结果验证改善。

options.label: 只测一次单个请求；它成功就说明活动全量结账不会超时
options.feedback: 单个请求没有施加目标负载，不能说明并发用户下的延迟、吞吐或错误率。

options.label: 把错误请求从统计里排除，只报告成功请求的平均响应时间
options.feedback: 排除失败会掩盖负载下的真实影响；错误率和响应时间都要按同一场景完整分析。

en.title: Before an event, checkout load testing shows 95th-percentile (p95) latency above threshold and rising errors. Which response is most useful?

options.label: Keep the scenario and metrics, locate the bottleneck, improve it, rerun, and compare the results
options.feedback: Correct. Load testing is useful when repeatable load and thresholds expose a bottleneck and the next run verifies the improvement.

options.label: Test one request once; if it succeeds, full-event checkout will not time out
options.feedback: One request applies no target load and cannot show latency, throughput, or errors under concurrency.

options.label: Exclude failed requests and report only the average response time of successful requests
options.feedback: Excluding failures hides the real impact under load; errors and latency must be analyzed for the same complete scenario.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请为活动结账流程设计一次负载测试：使用接近生产的独立环境和合成/脱敏数据，模拟浏览、加入购物车和结账，记录延迟、吞吐量和错误率，并先写清阈值。测试后告诉我瓶颈、原始结果和改善后的重复结果；不要把测试流量打到生产。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Design a load test for the event checkout flow. Use an isolated production-like environment with synthetic or sanitized data, simulate browsing, cart, and checkout, and define thresholds before recording latency, throughput, and error rate. After the test, report bottlenecks, original results, and repeated results after improvement; do not send test traffic to production.

learning.assumes: You know that slow pages, failed requests, and a system's processing capacity are related.
learning.outcome: You can state a load scenario, signals, thresholds, and the evidence needed to verify an improvement.

modules.title: How latency and errors cross thresholds as load increases
How a load test produces useful evidence

items.title: Make the test scenario repeatable
items.text: “Simulate many people” is not enough. State the user actions, load volume or request rate, duration, environment, and data type. A production-like environment with synthetic or sanitized data supports a realistic judgment without touching real customer data.

items.title: Let signals choose the next iteration
items.text: Record latency, throughput, and error rate and compare them with predefined thresholds. If checkout slows or fails as load rises, locate and improve the bottleneck, then rerun the same scenario. Better results show that this change helped, but only for the tested conditions.

items.title: A second scenario: an online class
items.text: Before class starts, simulate students joining the live room and submitting answers at the same time. At the target attendance, record join latency, submission throughput, and errors, then rerun under the same conditions after improvements.

modules.title: What it is not
modules.text: Load testing asks how a system behaves at a target or expected load. Stress testing generally pushes beyond that load to observe limits or failure modes. A passing load test covers only its environment, data, scenario, and time window; it cannot prove every production traffic pattern, dependency, or failure combination is safe.
